families_with_unknown_metric_direction.note: an argmax is undefined without a metric direction, so these families yield no declared winner at any cutoff and contribute only unresolved transitions; they are excluded from every winner-based and regret quantity by construction

noise_model.dispersion_source: defaulted for every call (substrate is pointer only)

regret.definition: regret at a cutoff is the direction-aware gap between the best value in the final-cutoff reference set and the declared method's best value in that same set, normalised by the reference spread; a declared method absent from the reference set takes the maximum in-set gap and is counted in the off-partition rate

oracles.protocol_gated: the largest valid comparison set at the final cutoff
oracles.ungated_naive: every entry at the final cutoff, protocol ignored; naive latest-max has regret zero against this oracle at the final cutoff by construction

bases.same_cutoff: each policy is averaged only over the cutoffs at which EVERY policy declared a winner, so the means cover identical cutoffs; this is the headline basis
bases.own_cutoffs: each policy is averaged over its own declared cutoffs; naive latest-max declares at cutoffs with no valid comparison set, where the gated policies decline and where naive does worst, so this basis is permissive toward gating

normalizing_baseline.note: naive_normalized reconciles a bounded metric reported as both a fraction and a percentage, then takes the argmax over every visible entry. It uses no comparability information, so the gap between it and protocol partitioning isolates the effect of checking conditions from the effect of fixing the unit artefact.

measured_gaps_only.note: same-cutoff basis, protocol-gated reference, restricted to cutoffs where the named method appears in the reference set; the absence penalty is excluded rather than assigned

absence_causes.note: absence from the SELECTED reference set, split by cause; a method in another valid comparison set is comparable there, so only the no-recorded-conditions and group-of-one causes are an absence of recoverable information

shortfall_paired_at_cutoff.note: both rules restricted to the cutoffs where each names a method present in the reference set, so the difference is not between two different subsets of cutoffs

basis_diagnostic.note: naive latest-max declares a winner at cutoffs where no valid comparison set exists and the gated policies decline; these are the cutoffs present in the own-cutoffs basis and absent from the same-cutoff basis

episode_decomposition.note: the unsettled decomposition with a within-band stretch counted once as an episode rather than once per cutoff; the transition-counted version is a different measurement and is kept under transitions

repeated_states_outcomes.note: an episode still inside the band at the final cutoff has no observed outcome; it is reported as ongoing and excluded from the recovery denominator rather than counted as a non-recovery

repeated_states.note: a family whose leading margin sits inside the band stays there until something changes, so every cutoff in that stretch is another weakened transition; first entries count distinct episodes

reversal_opportunities.note: an opportunity is a method already in the comparison set when the leader was declared that later receives a fresh measurement in that same set, so the recorded order between the two could have changed

protocol_drift_rate.definition: share of transitions at which the number of valid comparison sets grew
